newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM PGM futures surge by daily price limits.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM PGM futures surge by daily price limits.

text.p: Yen-based platinum group metals (PGMs) futures, except for the spot August contracts, ended sharply higher on Tuesday, following the rally in the New York market on Monday, traders said.
All palladium and platinum prices except for the August contracts were glued to their daily limits throughout the day.

Benchmark June palladium rose by its limit of 36 yen per gram to 755, while benchmark June platinum surged by its 50 yen limit to 1,594. "The rally was purely attributable to a large overhang of TOCOM short positions in palladium. There were basically few sellers around," one trader said.

The spot August PGM contract, which has no price limits, slipped from early highs on long-liquidation from trade houses in reaction to the TOCOM's announcement of measures to encourage short-covering, especially in palladium.

TOCOM said on Tuesday it will introduce a series of measures making it easier for market players to cover their short-positions, which include widening the PGM daily price limits. "The measures will certainly help promote short-covering, but sentiment in the PGM market is basically bullish," one analyst said. "The current price levels are not high enough for trade houses to sell," he said.
Although Japanese traders expected the August PGM shipments from Russia to arrive later this week, suspicion over the stability of Russian supplies remains.
Gold futures ended slightly weaker in directionless trade, tracking easier bullion prices, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from two yen to five yen per gram lower. Benchmark June was down five yen at 1,218 yen.

In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $322.90/323.40 per ounce at 0733 GMT, against $323.65/324.15 in New York on Monday. Benchmark June silver was up 0.3 yen per 10 grams at 174.8 yen. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk +81-3-3432-7431
